presentations.pitch: Strain & Form Console turns the trainer into a Whoop-style readiness console. Every call gets a Strain number (0 to 21) for how hard it was. Every rep gets a Form ring (recent practice vs long-run practice) that says whether they are sharp enough for a hard persona. Personal records are kept per persona. The pre-call briefing forecasts the load ('14 of 21, Hard') and names the record to beat. The live call is a dark night canvas: a strip with timer, strain ring and talk-ratio bar, a transcript in the middle, and a right-hand coach rail that shows one typed cue at a time (Ask, Objection, Pace, Step, Close). The rail also has a next-best-question chip, a six-step talk track and rubric rings that stay dashed until the final grader settles them. The library promises 240+ personas in 15 job families with strain tiers. The wizard has four entry points with redaction and exports a PR-ready file. Stack: Tailwind v4, shadcn on Base UI (I confirmed on the shadcn changelog that Base UI became the default in July 2026), Geist and Geist Mono, official OpenAI SDK, Realtime voice behind a VoiceProvider next to ElevenLabs. On the OpenAI fund angle, which I weighed explicitly: model chips on every surface, an Under the hood panel in every debrief (model, prompt version, tokens, cost), AGENTS.md, a Codex task prompt in the persona export, and Codex PR review on persona and schema PRs. That fits the program's stated uses (I confirmed PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows). The Codex story is described but not wired into CI.
presentations.strongest: Pre-call readiness is a genuinely useful learning idea: the rep knows the load before dialing, and the Strain forecast on persona cards replaces a vague difficulty label. The mobile live call is well considered (48px sticky strip, End always visible, single-line cue with a Why expand, quiet toggle, tab bar hidden). The Under the hood panel is the clearest audit trail for the OpenAI fund reviewer. Contrast was thought through (strain orange text swaps to #C2410C on light). Reduced motion degrades to instant numbers. Private PRs by default shows care for rep psychology.
presentations.weakest: The core vocabulary is the learning cost: Strain and Form have no stated formula, and Form needs about 42 days of history, so every new user sees empty 'New' rings on day one. In the live call a Strain ring is non-actionable chrome that competes with the coach for attention. The cue fades after 6 seconds, which fails WCAG 2.2.1 for slower readers and screen-reader users unless it can be paused or persisted, and it needs an aria-live strategy. Hold-to-talk is a sustained-press control that needs a toggle alternative for motor accessibility. Rings on every card and every screen add visual noise, and call-center reps may read Strain, Form and load flags as surveillance.
presentations.live_coaching_verdict: Slightly above baseline. Typed cues, a next-best-question chip, six-step talk-track progress, a talk-ratio band, provisional dashed rubric rings and an elevation timeline cover every item in the brief. Coach is a separate server channel, so the persona never hears advice. A rubric-only fallback if the coach times out is the right resilience choice. Held back by the 6-second auto-fade, the ornamental live Strain ring and an unmeasured 2.5s p95 latency target that the proposal itself says drops its score to 4 if missed.
presentations.persona_library_verdict: Above baseline on paper, with content risk. 240+ personas in 15 families, strain tiers, objection chips and a Form ring per card is the biggest catalogue claim in my set. The wizard is strong: four entry points, redaction of phone numbers, emails and names before any model call, a streaming persona card, rubric weights that must total 100, a 30-second test call and a PR-ready export. I discount it because 240 reviewed personas is a large content job (its own self-score falls to 4 under 100 shipped) and quality review is only a risk bullet.

presentations.pitch: Film Room Sideline treats every practice call as game film. One scrubbable timeline strip is the spine of the whole product: turns as coloured blocks, a playhead, and tagged moments (discovery, objection, pricing, close, filler, rapport) that appear live, then become the debrief. The live call is a dark three-column stage: timeline across the top, transcript with inline tag pills in the middle, and a 320px sideline HUD with six rubric meters, a talk-track checklist, one amber whisper cue at a time (20-second minimum gap, Esc to dismiss) and an objection alert chip, with two suggested replies by the composer. The debrief is timeline-first: click any tag and you get the quote, the transcript line and the coach note, and 'Replay this moment' starts a retake from that timestamp. The library is one versioned JSON pack (150+ target, about 40 hand-checked at launch) validated by a single zod schema shared by the wizard, importer and CI. The wizard has five steps with an editable extraction panel and PII stripping. Stack: shadcn on Radix, Tailwind v4, Motion, wavesurfer.js, Sora, Inter and JetBrains Mono. OpenAI fund angle: the repo's CI runs Codex CLI to review persona-pack PRs for schema, bias and rubric weights, and maintainer automation drafts release notes. I confirmed the fund pays for exactly this kind of use (PR review, maintainer automation, release workflows), so this is the best-aimed fund story of the five.
presentations.strongest: It has the best learning loop in the set. Score, quote, timestamp and Replay-this-moment are one click apart, and 'film room' is a metaphor a rep understands without onboarding (plain-word tags, no invented scores). Live-call ergonomics are the most accessibility-aware: the cue persists until dismissed instead of auto-fading, Esc dismisses it, the mobile cue is a swipe-away bottom sheet, targets are 44px, gutters are 16px, there is no horizontal scroll, and AA contrast ratios are written into the palette (17:1, 5.5:1, 12:1, 11:1). Radix gives focus traps and ARIA for sheets, sliders and tabs. Starting with a measured latency harness over recorded calls is the right engineering order. Consent and visibility labels on manager views are what a real sales org needs.
presentations.weakest: The 20-second minimum gap between cues can hold back help at exactly the moment an objection lands (the separate objection chip only partly covers this). The HUD packs a timeline strip, tag pills, six meters, a checklist, a cue and reply chips into one screen, which is dense under pressure. A waveform scrubber is not keyboard or screen-reader accessible by default (wavesurfer needs a keyboard and text alternative) and implies retained audio, which needs consent and storage rules. The timeline shrinks to a 48px strip on a phone and loses its value in text mode. The look is the least new (Sora and Inter kept, Hudl density can read sports-coded), the library is the least designed screen, and 'live and final scores cannot disagree' overstates what a rolling estimate can promise.
presentations.live_coaching_verdict: At or slightly above baseline (about 6.0). It covers whisper cue, objection alert, next-best question, checkpoint nudges and six live rubric meters where each number carries a transcript line that the debrief reuses. Cues go to the rep only, the persona never sees them, and in voice mode they can be spoken through a second headphone-only channel. It loses points for the throttled cue gap and because it is unproven until the recorded-call harness exists. Its real edge is what happens after the call: coaching evidence is pinned to moments, so the live coach and the debrief tell one story.
presentations.persona_library_verdict: Around baseline, slightly above on craft. One versioned pack, one zod schema, two scripted replies per persona for offline tests, fork-to-my-library, built-in vs community badges and an editable extraction panel in the wizard make it the most contributor- and CI-friendly library. It is held back by a short facet list (six jobs, eight industries, no real estate), only about 40 hand-checked personas at launch, and a plain filter-and-card layout. The wizard (URL, job description, ICP, CRM note or pasted call, PII stripped, PR-ready export) meets the brief well.

presentations.pitch: Signal Coach rebuilds the product on antd 5 plus Ant Design X, the AI-native component layer (Bubble, ThoughtChain, Prompts, Sender, Suggestion, Think). The app is light by default, and the live call is an always-dark cockpit scoped by darkAlgorithm: Bubble transcript with small coach tags under rep turns, a 360px right column that stays open with the current cue, a ThoughtChain showing why it fired, three next-best questions as Prompts, an amber objection alert and five provisional rubric bars. Its signature idea is 'cue with receipts': every cue opens to the trigger quote and the reasoning. Pre-call, the rep picks coach cadence (Quiet, Balanced, Intense) and toggles whisper cues, objection alerts, next-question prompts and talk-track progress. The library has URL-shareable facets, a coverage map of 12 jobs by 10 industries that shows empty cells as help wanted, and a wizard that streams its build as a ThoughtChain with a source badge on every generated field and a diff against the nearest template. OpenAI angle: Realtime as default voice with ElevenLabs as an adapter, a settings panel picking grader, coach and wizard models, a provenance chip on every AI output, AGENTS.md, Codex for PR review and release notes, and a stretch public grader-eval page against human-labelled transcripts. I checked its flagged risk: antd's own docs say v5 is mostly compatible with React 19 but needs a patch package (@ant-design/v5-patch-for-react-19) or unstableSetRender. So it is workable but not drop-in, and there is a known React 19 and Next 15 issue thread.
presentations.strongest: It is the only proposal that lets the rep control coaching density. The Quiet, Balanced and Intense cadence plus per-cue switches is the best learnability and pressure-management feature in the batch. It also gives the strongest trust model: the trigger quote and reasoning behind each cue let a rep check the coach. The coverage map is a smart contributor hook that no other design has. Filters live in the URL, the wizard shows its work, the manager view says reps see the same views, and the mobile cockpit has a one-line sticky cue that expands on tap and swipes away. The grader-eval page would be a credible thing for a fund panel to see.
presentations.weakest: The look is the problem, and the proposal admits it: default antd reads as enterprise admin, and it only works if a real design pass follows. antd's React 19 support needs a patch, CSS-in-JS can fight Tailwind preflight in a mixed migration, and the heavy stack sits on the live route. Ant Design X is young, and it is a locked npm package rather than owned, editable source, which is weaker for contributors than shadcn. On desktop the ThoughtChain is open next to the cue, three Prompts, an objection alert and five bars, which is a lot of reading mid-call. The library maths is inconsistent (12 jobs x 10 industries x 10 per cell is 1,200, not 120), and some job and industry cells make no sense.
presentations.live_coaching_verdict: Best of the five, about 6.7, but not by a mile. Typed items (whisper cue, objection alert, next question, talk-track step, criterion update with a confidence value), each with its trigger quote, provisional scores locked at debrief, user-set cadence, visual cues by default and opt-in headset-only audio. The 2-second target is stated, and Think shows while the coach works without blocking the rep. The cost is screen density and a coaching quality that still depends on a prompt and latency that no layout can fix.
presentations.persona_library_verdict: Slightly above baseline (about 6.0). Systematic coverage (12 jobs by 10 industries, every filter returns something, gaps visible and invitable) is a better contributor on-ramp than a raw count. Every persona is a JSON file on a published schema, and the wizard emits the same file. The wizard is the most explainable: streamed ThoughtChain steps with source quotes, a source badge per generated field, rubric weights that auto-balance to 100 and a diff against the nearest template. Content is 120 at launch and the scale claim is muddled, so I hold it near 6.

presentations.pitch: Signal Room Mission Control is a dark, instrument-grade cockpit with a light theme of equal weight. The live call has three zones. The left rail carries the call clock, a talk-ratio gauge that turns coral only after 20 seconds above 70 percent, a words-per-minute gauge, a tone bar and rubric meters that stay 'tentative' until the grader finds a verbatim quote. The centre is a speaker-lane transcript with per-turn waveforms drawn on canvas. The right rail is a coach rail with one amber whisper at a time, coral objection chips and tick-off checkpoints. The persona only talks; a separate GPT-4.1 mini coach channel emits typed events, each rendered in exactly one place. Reps can mute the coach or rate a cue 'useful' or 'noisy'. The debrief replays the call with evidence ticks on a waveform, and the library is a facet rail with counts and URL-shareable filters over 150 to 200 personas. The wizard drafts from a URL, document, transcript or form, cites a source line per field and stress-tests the draft with three simulated calls before saving. Stack: Tailwind v4, shadcn on Base UI (confirmed as the shadcn default since July 2026), Motion, Recharts, custom canvas waveform, OpenAI Realtime over WebRTC plus ElevenLabs. OpenAI angle: a model-stack strip on every call shows which model did voice, coaching and grading with latency and cost; AGENTS.md and token docs let Codex change the UI safely, and Codex PR review checks gallery snapshots.
presentations.strongest: Its best idea is deterministic, instant telemetry. Talk ratio and pace are measured on the client, so they keep working even if the LLM coach is late, and the coral threshold (20 seconds over 70 percent) is a calm, well-judged trigger instead of constant alarms. It is honest about uncertainty: meters stay tentative until a verbatim quote confirms them, and reps can mute the coach or rate cues useful or noisy to tune it. Accessibility intent is explicit: every gauge pairs colour with a text label and a shape, and every token pair gets an AA check. The wizard's three simulated stress-test calls are a distinctive quality gate, and the model-stack strip with latency and cost is a clear OpenAI showcase. Mobile gets a thumb-zone End and grade bar and a peek-and-expand cue sheet.
presentations.weakest: It is the densest live screen of the five: three gauges, a tone bar, five meters, per-turn waveforms, a transcript and a coach rail, all while the rep is talking. That is the wrong trade for live-call pressure, and the learnability bill (what do WPM and tone mean?) is high. The tone bar has no stated method and no validation. The coach cadence contradicts the target: rolling windows every 8 to 12 seconds versus a cue within 2 seconds of the turn ending, and the proposal never reconciles them. Replay on a waveform assumes retained audio and the consent and storage that come with it. Dark telemetry is a familiar AI-dashboard look that can feel like a trading terminal to new reps, and the coach channel does not exist yet.
presentations.live_coaching_verdict: Slightly above baseline (about 6.1). Typed events (cue, objection, checkpoint, talk-ratio alert, rubric evidence), each in exactly one place, plus talk-ratio and pace gauges that need no LLM, cover the brief and add real measurement. Cue rating and coach mute are good control surfaces. The score is capped by the unreconciled 8 to 12 second versus 2 second timing and by cognitive load: a rep cannot scan this much while holding a conversation.
presentations.persona_library_verdict: Slightly above baseline (about 6.2). 150 to 200 versioned personas across 12 to 15 jobs, six facets with counts, URL-shareable filters, fork to PR-ready files and a wizard that cites sources and stress-tests drafts with three simulated calls. The proposal's own risk note ('40 excellent beat 200 generic') is correct and leaves the real work, curation, undone. Pure content scale and cosmetic polish are roughly on par with the other proposals; the stress-test step is the differentiator.

presentations.pitch: Ambient Orb Call Room makes the app feel like a phone call. The live call is a full-viewport canvas with a shader-driven orb that breathes with the speaker's audio level, wrapped in a five-arc rubric halo (arc length is coverage, colour is the score band; dashed means estimate, solid means final). A single whisper cue in Instrument Serif italic rises, stays 6 seconds and fades. An objection turns the halo coral and adds a one-line pivot card. The chrome (rail, tab bar, controls) dissolves after 3 seconds without pointer or touch, and the transcript lives in a drag-up sheet. The orb then becomes the brand mark, persona avatar and debrief header across the product. Library: 120 seeded personas across 14 jobs, sections per job with View all (n), facets with counts, and a 3-second voice preview on every card. Wizard: a co-pilot split view where a persona card fills field by field with a source chip back to the pasted text, a duplicate check and a 60-second test call. Debrief has a moments timeline that replays 30 seconds. Team view uses readiness lanes (Not started, Developing, Ready) and a cited weekly AI digest. Stack: shadcn on Radix, Tailwind 3 kept (lowest migration cost), Motion, React Three Fiber with custom GLSL (three.js is already a dependency), Vaul sheets. OpenAI angle: a provenance line on every screen, cost per call in settings, optional second Realtime session whispering to the rep through headphones, a 'How this repo uses Codex' page and honest wording that selection is at OpenAI's discretion.
presentations.strongest: It is the only design that copes with live-call pressure by subtraction. A rep sees an orb, a timer and one whisper, which is the closest practice to a real call, and it is the easiest to learn for the call itself. Mobile ergonomics are the best in the set: 64px controls in the thumb zone, safe-area insets, a Vaul transcript sheet and a text mode that collapses the orb into a 96px header. The 3-second voice preview on persona cards is the right idea for a voice product, and the keyword-heuristic fallback still drives the halo with no API key. Keeping Tailwind 3 and the existing three.js dependency makes phase 1 the cheapest migration of the five. The readiness-lane team view with a cited digest is distinctive.
presentations.weakest: It hides the very things a coaching product must keep visible. Controls that fade after 3 seconds hurt keyboard, switch and motor-impaired users and anyone who glances away, and a cue that fades after 6 seconds fails WCAG 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 timing expectations unless it can be paused or persisted. The rubric halo has no numbers and no criterion labels, so a rep has to decode arcs by colour, and colour-only score bands are an accessibility gap. No captions for voice mode are specified. The orb is the exact element the brief diagnoses as generic, and the dark orb is the most familiar AI-voice cliche. Next-best-question is not a named cue, coaching depth is thin, and WebGL on low-end phones is a live risk.
presentations.live_coaching_verdict: Just below baseline (4.9). Whisper cue, objection pivot, talk-track dots and a live halo technically cover the brief, and the dashed-to-solid estimate and no-key heuristic fallback are good. But the live score is illegible (unlabelled, numberless arcs), the cue disappears on a timer, the controls vanish, and there is no talk-ratio, pace or named next-best-question surface. A rep who looks away misses the help, so I rate it as falling just short of coaching that actually works.
presentations.persona_library_verdict: Slightly below to at baseline (about 5.4). 120 personas across 14 jobs with job sections, facets with counts, YAML files validated by zod in CI, and a unique voice preview. The wizard (paste or URL, field-by-field streaming with source chips, duplicate check, 60-second test call, export as PR) is good. It is the thinnest catalogue of the five and its job list omits SaaS as an explicit job; the browsing UI is a standard card grid.
